weekly.markdown:
# Trencher Weekly Review — Week of Sep 22–28, 2026

## 1. Headline

**17 closed picks, 8 wins / 9 losses (47% win rate), P&L −$21.71 on $850 staked (−2.6%).** Not closer to real money yet on the hard numbers, but the *mechanism* that matters most — exits — is working: actual exits averaged 0.97× stake vs. 0.44× if we'd naively held to 24h and 0.09× at 72h. The problem this week isn't exit discipline, it's entry quality (too many picks that needed the stop-loss at all) and a scoring model that may be over-weighting the wrong signals.

## 2. Pick table

| Symbol | Chain | Score | 1h | 6h | 24h | 72h | P&L | Exit reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PUMPPO | sol | 90 | 1.19 | 1.15 | 0.93 | 0.03 | +7.26 | no move 12h |
| UPTOBER | sol | 88 | 1.45 | 0.86 | 1.51 | 0.90 | +10.02 | trailing stop |
| PIPEJEAN | sol | 88 | 1.46 | 0.01 | 0.01 | – | −0.78 | trailing stop |
| AI | sol | 78 | 0.93 | 0.34 | 0.11 | 0.07 | +13.48 | trailing stop |
| UPTOBER | sol | 79 | 1.14 | 0.77 | 0.98 | 0.59 | −13.36 | no move 12h |
| BOARDCAT | sol | 96 | 0.20 | 0.01 | 0.01 | 0.01 | +17.86 | trailing stop |
| NUVEX | sol | 92 | 1.54 | 0.12 | 0.06 | – | +12.84 | trailing stop |
| OnlyJeans | sol | 88 | 1.03 | 0.01 | 0.01 | – | −21.56 | stop loss |
| LESTER | sol | 76 | 0.97 | 0.75 | 0.52 | – | −21.39 | stop loss |
| DELREY | sol | 76 | 0.68 | 0.77 | 1.60 | – | +11.57 | trailing stop |
| 7 | sol | 89 | 1.71 | 1.34 | 1.70 | – | +41.60 | trailing stop |
| SPLIT | sol | 85 | 2.32 | 0.52 | 0.09 | – | −21.59 | stop loss |
| CATSTR | sol | 88 | 0.93 | 0.26 | – | – | −22.89 | stop loss |
| KARDASHEV | sol | 80 | 0.53 | 0.61 | – | – | −21.63 | stop loss |
| x/acc | sol | 92 | 0.02 | 0.02 | – | – | −23.17 | stop loss |
| MM | sol | 78 | 0.33 | – | – | – | −22.05 | stop loss |
| MAGACOIN | sol | 72 | 0.01 | – | – | – | +32.08 | trailing stop |

Notable: SPLIT was up 2.3× at 1h but still ended a stop-loss loser — we have no way to lock in a fast early spike (see notebook).

## 3. Rule report card

| Rule | n | rug% | doubled% | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| too few holders | 1403 | 71 | 1 | working well — blocks almost nothing but rugs |
| owner can mint new coins | 232 | 78 | 0 | working well |
| creator/owner holds X% | 194 | 84 | 1 | working well |
| Single/Top10/High ownership rules | 55/42/41 | 90–91 | 2 | working well |
| creator holds X% | 57 | 88 | 9 | good |
| Low Liquidity | 77 | 84 | 10 | good |
| many linked wallets | 115 | 77 | 9 | good |
| Large Amount of LP Unlocked | 263 | **94** | 30 | high doubled%, but rug% so extreme it's clearly earning its keep |
| only X% liquidity locked/burned | 371 | 83 | 24 | same pattern — high rug%, keep as-is |
| top 10 wallets hold X% | 245 | 86 | 27 | same pattern — keep as-is |
| contract not verified | 42 | **45** | 12 | weakest rug rate of any n≥20 rule — closest thing to "too tight," but not strong enough (still blocks ~half rugs) to propose loosening |
| Mint/Freeze authority, honeypot, sell tax, etc. | ≤10 each | — | — | **n < 20, not judgeable yet** |

No rule this week clears the bar for a loosening proposal (would need low rug% *and* high doubled% together — closest is "contract not verified" but 45% rug is still too costly to touch).

## 4. Scoring

**Score buckets** (candidates that passed safety, by score):

| Bucket | n | median 24h | rug% | doubled% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50–59 | 37 | 0.00 | 84 | 11 |
| 60–69 | 50 | 0.07 | 66 | 18 |
| **70–79** | 88 | **0.22** | **48** | 18 |
| 80+ | 93 | 0.03 | 81 | 13 |

Score is **not monotonic** — 70–79 clearly beats both 60–69 and 80+. The 80+ bucket looks almost as bad as 50–59. min_score=60 still clears the worst bucket, so no change there, but something in how the top scores are composed is dragging them down.

**Components** (n=274 scored candidates, high vs low half):

| Component | high n | high rug%/doubled% | low n | low rug%/doubled% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| momentum | 90 | 73% / 11% | 184 | 65% / **18%** |
| holders | 124 | **90%** / 16% | 150 | 49% / 15% |
| liquidity | 0 | — | 274 | 68% / 16% (no discrimination — everything fell in "low") |
| buyer_breadth | 0 | — | 274 | 68% / 16% (identical to liquidity — looks like these two aren't actually separating candidates) |
| social | 141 | 67% / 16% | 133 | 69% / 16% (no signal either way) |
| survival | 21 | 62% / 10% | 253 | 68% / 16% (n=21 barely meets threshold, weak signal) |

Two findings stand out with solid n (≥90 each side):
- **Momentum is inverted**: high-momentum-scored coins double *less* often (11% vs 18%) and hit +50% less often (14% vs 26%) than low-momentum ones. Classic "buying the local top" pattern.
- **Holders is inverted more sharply**: high-holders-score coins rug 90% of the time vs. 49% for low. Whatever this component measures (likely holder growth rate, not raw count), it looks like it's picking up bot/wash-traded holder counts that precede rugs.

This is a plausible explanation for why the 80+ score bucket underperforms 70–79 — the top bucket is likely stacked with coins that scored well on momentum/holders for the wrong reasons.

**Stage funnel**: pick (n=10) median 24h 0.11 vs pass (n=28) 0.09 — Claude's picks edge out its passes, consistent with the go-live check, but n=10 for picks is too small to trust fully.

**Entry signal — "5-min spike over 20%"**: yes (n=32) and no (n=198) have essentially identical median_24h (0.08 both) and down40@1h (51% vs 49%). No separation, and the yes-side n is under the 40-per-side bar anyway. **Not recommending this signal for use.**

## 5. Exits

| | avg x | 
|---|---|
| Actual exits (n=17) | **0.974** |
| Hold to 24h | 0.442 |
| Hold to 72h | 0.094 |

Exit logic (stop-loss/trailing/no-move) is clearly adding value — more than doubling average outcome vs. a naive 24h hold, and 10× vs a 72h hold. This is the strongest working part of the system right now.

## 6. Go-live checklist

| Check | Pass? | Value |
|---|---|---|
| ≥30 closed paper picks | ❌ | 17 |
| Total paper P&L positive | ❌ | −21.72 |
| Win rate ≥35% | ✅ | 47% |
| Profitable 2 of last 3 weeks | ❌ | −32 / +10 (and this week negative) |
| Picks beat passes (median 24h) | ✅ | 0.11 vs 0.09 |

Missing: more volume, and a positive-P&L week. The entry side (score composition) is the more likely lever than the exit side.

## 7. Changes this week

Two changes, both backed by n≥90-per-side signal from the score-component breakdown, both small steps within range, both directly testable next week:

1. **weights.momentum 1.0 → 0.7** — high-momentum-scored candidates underperformed low-momentum ones (doubled 11% vs 18%, up50 14% vs 26%, n=90/184). Hypothesis: the momentum component is currently rewarding coins that have already spiked (buying near a local top). Lowering its weight should shift picks toward less-extended entries. **Confirms if**: next week's picks show higher median 24h / up50 rate and momentum's high/low split narrows or flips.

2. **weights.holders 1.0 → 0.7** — high-holders-scored candidates rugged far more than low (90% vs 49%, n=124/150). Hypothesis: this component is picking up inflated/bot-driven holder counts that precede rugs rather than genuine distribution. **Confirms if**: rug_pct among picks/passes drops and the holders high/low rug gap narrows next week.

Holding steady on min_score, stop_loss_pct, and all safety-rule thresholds — none showed a strong enough loosening case, and the exit config is already outperforming a naive hold by a wide margin, so no reason to touch it yet.

---

## Notebook (rewritten)

**Week 1 findings:**
- Exit logic (stop-loss 40% / trailing 30% / no-move 12h) is working well: actual avg exit 0.97× vs hold-24h 0.44× vs hold-72h 0.09×. Don't touch these yet — they're the strongest part of the system.
- Score is **not monotonic**: 70–79 bucket (median 24h 0.22, rug 48%) beats 80+ (median 0.03, rug 81%). Root cause hypothesis: momentum and holders components are inversely predictive at the high end (see below). **Changed both weights 1.0→0.7 this week — watch if the 80+ bucket improves relative to 70–79 next week.**
- `liquidity` and `buyer_breadth` score components show **identical stats (n=274 "low", n=0 "high")** — suspicious, looks like they may not be computing distinct values or the split threshold is broken. Can't fix from tuning — flag to owner to check the scoring code.
- `social` and `survival` components show no discriminating power so far (survival n=21 is borderline, worth re-checking with more data before concluding).
- "5-min spike over 20%" entry signal shows zero separation (yes vs no nearly identical on median_24h and down40@1h) — not worth enabling even once n grows, unless the picture changes.
- SPLIT hit 2.3× at 1h then got stopped out for a loss — no mechanism exists to lock in fast early spikes. **Idea for owner**: a partial take-profit rule (e.g., sell 50% if price ≥2× within first hour) isn't in the current tunable list; worth building.
- `contract not verified` rule has the weakest rug rate of any n≥20 safety rule (45%) — watchlist for a future loosening proposal, but not yet (still blocks real rugs half the time).
- Go-live blockers: need 13 more closed picks to hit 30, and a P&L-positive week. Entry quality (not exits) is the lever — see weight changes above.
- Next week: check whether momentum/holders weight cuts shift the score-bucket ordering back toward monotonic and reduce stop-loss frequency without hurting win rate.

Paper trading only — not financial advice.
